messages:
amal: Hey team — quick onboarding snag. My app fails to connect to local Redis: TLS required by config but my compose stack doesn't have certs set up. Error: 'WRONGPASS or client sent AUTH, but TLS is required' Anyone set up TLS for local dev before?

devex-bot: Hi Amal! See dev docs on dev redis setup: https://internal.redwood.dev/dev-setup/redis (dev tip: you can toggle REDIS_REQUIRE_TLS in .env) :robot_face:

sophie: For local development we usually disable TLS. Add REDIS_REQUIRE_TLS=false to your .env.local and run `docker-compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.override.yml up` — quick and dirty.

tom: If you want to run Redis with TLS locally, we spin up stunnel in compose. Example override (docker-compose.override.yml):
```yaml
services:
  redis:
    image: redis:7
    command: ["redis-server", "/usr/local/etc/redis/redis.conf", "--tls-port", "6379", "--port", "0"]
    volumes:
      - ./devcerts/redis:/etc/redis/certs:ro
  stunnel:
    image: alpine/stunnel
    volumes:
      - ./devcerts/redis:/etc/stunnel:ro
    ports:
      - \"6379:6379\"
```
You can create self-signed certs with `openssl` or `mkcert`.

natalie: Also note: don't commit devcerts to repo. We put a README in infra/dev-certs/ and use .gitignore. Production settings must still enforce TLS and proper certs. If you're on mac+colima, watch out for hostnames — use 127.0.0.1 in `tls-server-name` or adjust SANs.

sophie: If you just want to skip TLS for now, add this to docker-compose.override.yml and .env:
```yaml
redis:
  environment:
    REDIS_REQUIRE_TLS: \"false\"
```
Then `docker compose down && docker compose up --build`. :thumbsup:

amal: Thanks all — disabled TLS in .env.local and it works. Linking this thread to onboarding doc so future hires see it. :tada:

devex-bot: Linked to onboarding onboarding:redis-tls-note in knowledge base.
